extraction.Name: James G. Dixon
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his 160 acre allotment when it was issued, but he was told by the Indian Agency at Pine Ridge, that it would be assessed for taxes, and finally be sold for them, if he did not take it, so he accepted
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: in 1919, he sold it to his father, John H. Dixon, for $1000.00, receiving $500.00 in cash, and $500.00 in trade, stock
extraction.Buyer: John H. Dixon (father) for $1000.00, $500.00 in cash and $500.00 in trade stock
extraction.Occupation/Income: he farms a small, rented farm, in summer, and, in winter, he hunts coyotes, these two sources of supply is his only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has pretty good health; has a wife who is so badly done up with the rheumatism that she cannot get around; has three children to support with good health; considers $1000.00 a pretty slim price for his allotment; father promised to deed it back but was accidentally killed before he could do so; has never received any help from the County, State or the United States Government; document sworn November 30, 1928; allotment was 160 acres
